title: KV Cache, Flash Attention, and Inference Optimization

questions.question: Long conversations recompute everything per token without reuse. What must persist across decode steps?
options: Only the newest query vector
A single averaged scalar
Nothing; recompute all each time
Past keys and values for the full prefix
questions.explanation: Recompute is quadratic waste. This lesson caches keys and values for reuse.

questions.question: For N=10, how many cumulative attention operations does decode_naive report?
questions.explanation: The loop counts 1+2+...+10 = 10*11/2 = 55 prefix positions attended across all decode steps.

questions.question: What numerical idea lets tiled_softmax_dot combine blocks without storing one full score row?
options: It carries a running maximum and normalization sum while rescaling the partial weighted value sum
It replaces softmax with an unnormalized sum of raw dot products
It drops every score below zero before normalizing
It recomputes the complete attention matrix after each tile
questions.explanation: new_m, exp_old, and s rescale previous contributions when a later tile has a larger score maximum, preserving the softmax result.

questions.question: What is the formula implemented by kv_cache_bytes(N, n_layers, n_heads_kv, d_head, dtype=2)?
options: N+n_layers+n_heads_kv+d_head+dtype bytes
2*N*n_layers*n_heads_kv*d_head*dtype bytes
N*n_layers*d_head divided by n_heads_kv
2*N*dtype independent of layers and head width
questions.explanation: The leading 2 accounts for separate K and V tensors; the remaining factors count positions, layers, KV heads, head width, and bytes per element.

questions.question: Why can decode_cached avoid rebuilding earlier K and V projections even though each query still attends to a growing prefix?
options: It stores only attention weights, which are independent of K and V
It attends only to the newest token and ignores the prefix
It appends each new K/V pair once and reuses the cache for later attention calls
It uses top-k sampling to remove old keys
questions.explanation: decode_cached appends the current pair and passes cache.K/cache.V to attention_full; the prefix representations are not recomputed.

questions.question: What should happen when tiled_softmax_dot is run with tile=1 versus tile=32 on the demo's 10 keys?
options: The output dimension changes from 8 to 32
Only tile=1 is normalized; tile=32 returns raw values
Tile=32 sees no keys because it is larger than the sequence
Both should agree with attention_full up to floating-point reassociation
questions.explanation: Tile size changes how blocks are accumulated, not the mathematical attention; the demo reports tiny maximum absolute differences for each size.
